arXiv:2610.41721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In quantum computing, the readout always carries finite-shot sampling noise. item.description:

Real-time telemetry diagnostics and predictive anomaly tracking in nuclear reactor cores present a fundamental computational dilemma: high-fidelity numerical neutronics and thermal-hydraulics solvers are too computationally prohibitive for sub-second edge evaluation, whereas conventional black-box deep learning architectures violate physical conservation bounds and lack operational determinism. Simultaneously, transmitting safetycritical nuclear operational data to public cloud infrastructure introduces acute cyber-physical security vectors that breach strict operational air-gaps. item.title: Quantum-Geometric Subgap Second-Harmonic Generation in PT-Symmetric Antiferromagnetic Insulators
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Shakeel Ahmad, Fei Xue
arXiv:2610.41167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although quantum geometry plays an established role in electronic transport and optical responses, the contribution of the time-reversal-odd Riemannian connection to fully subgap responses remains less explored. Here we identify intrinsic second-harmonic generation in PT-symmetric antiferromagnets, predominantly governed by the real sector of the interband Hermitian connection and arising entirely from virtual interband transitions. In bilayer MnBi₂Te₄, the response persists in trivial phases but is enhanced in the layer-Chern phase and reverses sign with Néel order, offering a probe of quantum geometry and phase-sensitive readout of antiferromagnetic order without mobile carriers or real excitations.

item.description:

👤 Carla Cotea, Stefan Balauca, Andreea Arusoaie
Training parameterized quantum circuits requires balancing optimization progress with limited evaluation budgets and the statistical uncertainty of near-term quantum hardware. We evaluate a suite of gradient-based, stochastic, and derivative-free optimizers across combinatorial optimization using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), supervised quantum machine learning using Iris classification and a quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN) for binary MNIST classification, and quantum chemistry using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) for molecular hydroge…

item.title: MixFunn: A Neural Architecture for Differential Equations with Mixed Functions and Second-Order Interactions
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Tiago de Souza Farias, Gubio Gomes de Lima, Jonas Maziero, Celso Jorge Villas-Boas
We introduce MixFunn, a neural network architecture designed for modeling solutions of differential equations. The proposed architecture combines two main components: (i) mixed-function neurons, which employ a set of predefined activation functions to enrich the functional representation, and (ii) second-order neurons, which explicitly incorporate interactions between different neurons. Together, these elements aim to increase representational flexibility while maintaining a compact model structure. We evaluate MixFunn on a set of differential equation problems, including the damped and forced harmonic oscillator, the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation, and the quantum infinite square well. Attractor dynamics underlie the collective computation of neural networks. Recurrent connections between biological neurons can give rise to stable states towards which network activity relaxes, allowing parallel operation without global coordination while preserving robustness. Implementing physical systems with reliable attractor dynamics is therefore important both for understanding biological intelligence and for developing bio-inspired computing systems. However, parallel physical evolution introduces dynamical challenges. Concurrent evolution of artificial neurons can support rapid collective relaxation, but can also prevent the network from settling. item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Jingbo Wu, Shaofeng Li, Yafeng Yang, Liuxi Li, Zhipeng Wang
Torque ripple caused by uneven torque transfer during phase commutation limits the low-speed steady-state performance of switched reluctance motors (SRMs). This paper proposes a control strategy that uses iterative learning control (ILC) to optimize the torque sharing function (TSF). Starting from a cosine TSF, the method uses the torque error recurring within each electrical cycle to update the TSF in the commutation region from one cycle to the next. The resulting reference torque distribution progressively approaches the actual electromagnetic torque response, thereby improving torque transfer between phases. Dahal Jeet is a four-player partnership card game played daily across the Terai- Madhesh region of Nepal, in which only the four tens score. Its objective is lexicographic rather than additive: a majority of tens decides most hands, trick count the rest.
